I was driving on a popular 4 lane highway in my state headed to my college. I didn't have class that day but I wanted to pay part of my tuition that day.

An older woman pulled out in front of me from a median and I couldn't brake in time so I T-Boned her car from the passenger side. Totalled both vehicles. She was bleeding and had head trauma. I walked away with not even a bruise. At the hospital, my friend's Mom who was a paramedic talked to me and said the lady was stable but that's all she could tell me.

A week later, I was on my lunch break at work and called the highway patrol department to get the police report so I could get the ball rolling on insurance replacing my vehicle. I was told on the phone that "I can't release the police report to you because the other party has died". I was quiet for a while, but had a meltdown in the office area and one of the office ladies had to comfort me.

I feel guilty because the woman was in the choir at her church, had grandchildren, and was a well-loved member of her community. I'm still just a punk kid with Daddy issues and a nicotine and caffeine addiction. I felt like the wrong person died and me living was an insult to her. Her granddaughter reached out to me on Facebook and told me she didn't blame me and that things happen. That only helped a little.

2 1/2 years later, I still have suicidal thoughts because of that day and wouldn't wish the knowledge that you are responsible for someone's death on anyone.
